overall: A curious, dry explainer voice, someone who knows this county and is walking you through how the thing works, never selling it. Energy opens plain and curious, lifts a little through the mechanism, drops hard on the acreage, and finishes lower and more certain than the middle.

lines.text: A thin curl of smoke rises off the Panhandle grass. Up on a tower, two cameras turn and lock onto it.
lines.intent: Open on the picture, quiet and observational
lines.note: Plain and unhurried. Weight on smoke in the first sentence and lock in the second. No lift at the end of either sentence.

lines.text: There is a reason they are up there. The Smokehouse Creek fire started in Hutchinson County near Stinnett and became the largest wildfire in state history.
lines.intent: Turn from image to stakes, a dry setup
lines.note: First sentence short and wry, a small beat after it. Stinnett is said STIN-et, two syllables, stress on the first, said like a local who has driven through. Weight lands on largest.

lines.text: It burned roughly 1,058,482 acres. Xcel Energy said its facilities appeared to have been involved.
lines.intent: Land the central fact, then the attribution, flat and exact
lines.note: Quietest line of the opening and the heaviest fact. Read 1,058,482 acres slowly and plainly, digit group by digit group, no lift on acres, then a full beat. The Xcel sentence stays level and careful, no accusation in the tone.

lines.text: So Xcel teamed up with a company called Pano AI. By last November, there were 57 camera stations across the Panhandle, each on top of a communication tower.
lines.intent: Release into the response, the story starts moving
lines.note: Step up from the drop, brisk and matter of fact. Weight on Pano AI and on 57. Spell the letters of AI out cleanly.

lines.text: Each station sweeps a full 360 degrees every minute. It watches about 10 miles in each direction.
lines.intent: Explain the mechanism in two clean facts
lines.note: Even and clear, a teacher's pace. Weight on every minute and on 10 miles. The two sentences are a matched pair, same shape, no rise.

lines.text: Its AI is hunting one thing. Smoke. When it finds a grey smudge on the horizon, it flags it.
lines.intent: Narrow the focus, a small dry punch
lines.note: Smoke is a one word sentence, set apart and said flat. Grey smudge slightly slower, almost visual. Flags it lands low and quick.

lines.text: A flag is not a fire, though. So a human analyst checks it first.
lines.intent: Add the human check, a mild correction
lines.note: Dry aside on though, not a lecture. Weight on human.

lines.text: Then a second tower turns its eyes the same way. Where the two sightlines cross, the map can get exact coordinates.
lines.intent: Show the trick, the payoff of the method
lines.note: Slight forward motion on the first sentence. Slow a hair on cross, then land exact coordinates plainly with a quiet satisfaction, not a flourish.

lines.text: Pano calls 911. The closest fire department gets the live stream, and a brush truck rolls.
lines.note: Short and concrete. 911 said as nine one one, flat. Rolls is the soft landing, no lift.

lines.text: Here is the catch. Xcel's Reeves warns responders that a lot of these alerts will turn out to be nothing.
lines.intent: Turn to the cost, the honest complication
lines.note: Drop in energy and pace on the catch, confiding. Weight on nothing, said almost shrugging.

lines.text: Most people are okay with that, he says. They want to know everything that is going on.
lines.note: Reported voice, relaxed and a little amused, sounds like a quote and not a statement of the narrator's own. Weight on everything.

lines.text: Some cameras look over towns, though. Those pixelate anything built, houses and all.
lines.intent: Raise the privacy wrinkle, brief and matter of fact
lines.note: Light dry touch on though again but a different shape than before, less wry. Weight on pixelate. Houses and all trails off lower.

lines.text: Somebody pays for all of it. Xcel paid up front and will ask regulators to recover that cost, and it planned 68 more under a $490 million resiliency plan.
lines.note: Open with the short sentence at conversational weight. Then the long sentence in an even run, weight on recover and on 68. Say 490 million dollars flat, no lift on the figure.

lines.text: None of it puts out a fire. It buys a head start, and then somebody still has to drive toward the smoke.
lines.note: Lowest and most settled line of the read. None of it puts out a fire said flat and sure. Head start slightly warmer. Final clause slows and falls on smoke, finality with no moral on top, then silence.
